Class ClientHandlerSocket

java.lang.Object
it.polimi.ingsw.network.server.ClientHandler
it.polimi.ingsw.network.server.socket.ClientHandlerSocket
All Implemented Interfaces:
VirtualView, DisconnectionListener, ModelObserver, Runnable
public class ClientHandlerSocket extends ClientHandler implements VirtualView, Runnable, DisconnectionListener
Server-side socket handler for a connected client.

Implements Runnable to be executed by the server's thread pool. The run() method initializes I/O streams, then enters a read loop deserializing incoming ClientMessage and routing them to ClientMessageVisitor.

All outgoing ServerMessage pass through ClientHandler.sendAsync(CheckedRunnable), queued on the single-threaded executor for ordered, non-concurrent writes to the output stream.

A health check thread periodically sends PingMessage. If no messages arrive within TIMEOUT_LIMIT milliseconds, the connection is deemed lost and disconnection is triggered.

Design

The base class entirely manages disconnection flag, message executor, and async pattern. This class handles only socket-specific logic: I/O streams, Java serialization, timestamp-based timeouts.

    • ClientHandlerSocket

      public ClientHandlerSocket(Socket socket, MatchManager matchManager)
      Creates a new socket handler. The nickname is initially unknown and will be set by onLogin(String) after login.

      Does not start the health check; it is started by onLogin(String) once the nickname is available for logging.

      Parameters:

      matchManager - the match coordinator

  • Method Details

    • setup

      public void setup() throws IOException
      Initializes object I/O streams from the underlying socket.

      The ObjectOutputStream must be created first, as the ObjectInputStream constructor on the remote side blocks until the stream header is received.

      Throws:
      IOException - if streams cannot be opened

    • run

      public void run()
      Main loop executed by the thread pool thread.

      Calls setup(), then reads ClientMessage objects in a loop, dispatches them via ClientHandler.onClientMessage(ClientMessage), and updates lastMessageReceivedTime on each successful read. On IOException or ClassNotFoundException, the loop exits, and disconnection is triggered.

      Specified by:
      run in interface Runnable

    • startHealthCheck

      protected void startHealthCheck()
      Starts the transport-specific health check thread.

      Called by subclass constructors after initializing network resources (e.g., RMI stubs, socket streams).

      Starts a daemon thread that every ClientHandler.PING_INTERVAL ms sends a PingMessage and checks for activity within TIMEOUT_LIMIT ms. If the timeout is exceeded, disconnection is triggered.

      Called by onLogin(String) after the nickname is known, enabling meaningful thread names for logging.

      Specified by:
      startHealthCheck in class ClientHandler

    • handleTransportError

      protected void handleTransportError(Exception e)
      Handles a transport error during asynchronous send.

      Typically marks the client as disconnected and notifies the appropriate listener (e.g., DisconnectionListener, MatchManager).

      Delegates to handleDisconnection(String) with the current nickname, consolidating cleanup logic in a single place.

      Specified by:
      handleTransportError in class ClientHandler
      Parameters:
      e - the exception (RemoteException for RMI, IOException for socket)

    • tryMarkDisconnected

      protected boolean tryMarkDisconnected()
      Marks the handler as disconnected in an idempotent manner and shuts down the ClientHandler.messageSender.

      Subclasses owning additional executors or resources must override this method, call super.tryMarkDisconnected() first, and proceed only if it returns true: 

      @Override
protected synchronized boolean tryMarkDisconnected() {
    if (!super.tryMarkDisconnected()) return false;
    myExecutor.shutdownNow();
    return true;
}

      In addition to base cleanup, closes I/O streams and the TCP socket.

      Overrides:
      tryMarkDisconnected in class ClientHandler
      Returns:
      true if this thread was first to mark disconnection; false if already disconnected

    • handleDisconnection

      public void handleDisconnection(String nickname)
      Marks the client as disconnected, notifies the MatchManager, and closes resources. Idempotent.

      If the client disconnects before completing login the nickname is null; in that case the socket is closed but MatchManager is not notified, since the player was never registered.

      Specified by:
      handleDisconnection in interface DisconnectionListener
      Specified by:
      handleDisconnection in interface VirtualView
      Parameters:
      nickname - the player's nickname, or null if not yet logged in

    • closeStreams

      private void closeStreams()
      Closes I/O streams and the TCP socket. Any IOException during cleanup is logged and ignored.

    • onLogin

      public void onLogin(String nickname)
      Called after successful login: stores the nickname and starts the health check.

      Note: the nickname field is final in the base class. In the socket protocol the nickname is not known at construction time, so this method must be called exactly once immediately after login.

      Specified by:
      onLogin in interface VirtualView
      Parameters:
      nickname - the registered player nickname
